_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); athletic footwear and apparel signals

pit_profile.why: NIKE: 'NIKE is the largest seller of athletic footwear and apparel in the world', and 'Nearly all of our products are manufactured by independent contractors' (its own FY2025 10-K); the industry 'is highly competitive on a worldwide basis', 'including adidas, Anta, ASICS, Deckers, Li Ning, lululemon athletica, New Balance, On, Puma, Under Armour and V.F. Corporation, among others', and 'the relative popularity of various sports and fitness activities and changing design trends affect the demand for our products': a demand and fashion risk, not an obsolescence one

theme_watch.reason: Live: NIKE's own FY2025 10-K says 'Our NIKE Direct operations, both through our digital commerce operations and retail stores, also compete with multi-brand retailers, which sell our products through their digital platforms and physical stores, and with digital commerce platforms.' At the same time it sells online itself, though less: 'declines in NIKE Brand Digital sales of 20% from $12.1 billion in fiscal 2024 to $9.6 billion in fiscal 2025'. The stock trades at 20.4x FY26E — a discount to its own history. Re-file as DISRUPTION_EXPOSED (ECOMMERCE) only if dated evidence shows the market pricing the shift away from physical retail into NIKE's own sales specifically.

classification.quality_note: NIKE: 'NIKE is the largest seller of athletic footwear and apparel in the world', and 'Nearly all of our products are manufactured by independent contractors' (its own FY2025 10-K); the industry 'is highly competitive on a worldwide basis', 'including adidas, Anta, ASICS, Deckers, Li Ning, lululemon athletica, New Balance, On, Puma, Under Armour and V.F. Corporation, among others', and 'the relative popularity of various sports and fitness activities and changing design trends affect the demand for our products': a demand and fashion risk, not an obsolescence one. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.75x; -15% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.61; conservative 2yr +69%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -45.3%/yr (worst year FY16-FY25 ex-FY18, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +-1.2%/yr (Q3 rev ex-FX + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr ex-FY18 median

BULL.desc: EPS +0.0%/yr (FY16-FY25 ex-FY18 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +53.1%/yr (best 2-yr run FY16-FY25 ex-FY18); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: NKE (retrospective, 2026-05-08) ◎ ACCUMULATE — Ratio B 0.75x (66.0% downside to Bear $15 / +88.0% upside to Bull $83) | Adj composite 2.35 vs market 1.74: gap +0.61 [UNDERVALUED] | -15% above the EPP floor $52 (24x FY26E $2.16) | Conservative 2-yr case: +69.1% total (+34.6%/yr) | At 20.4x FY26E the 15% hurdle price $58 sits at or below the BASE case; futures orders not reported for Q3 FY26, forward revenues -3% (Q3 FY26 revenue ex-currency); e-commerce is live and company-acknowledged; no dated evidence ties the multiple to it.
